title: The abc Conjecture
exact_target: Apart from finitely many exceptions for each fixed positive epsilon, is c at most the radical of abc raised to the power one plus epsilon, when a and b are coprime positive integers with a+b=c?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Shared notation.}$\mathbb N=\{1,2,\ldots\}$, and $\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q,\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ denote the integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers. Any other conventions are specified locally.


For a positive integer \(n\), define its radical by
\[
 \operatorname{rad}(n)=\prod_{\substack{p\mid n\\p\text{ prime}}}p,
 \qquad \operatorname{rad}(1)=1.
\]
The product counts each distinct prime divisor only once.
If \(a+b=c\) and \(\gcd(a,b)=1\), the three positive integers
\(a,b,c\) are pairwise coprime.
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For every real number \(\varepsilon>0\), is there a constant
\(C_\varepsilon>0\) such that every triple of positive integers
\((a,b,c)\) with \(a+b=c\) and \(\gcd(a,b)=1\) satisfies
\[
 c\le C_\varepsilon\,\operatorname{rad}(abc)^{\,1+\varepsilon}?
\]
Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), are there only finitely many
such triples with \(c>\operatorname{rad}(abc)^{1+\varepsilon}\)? \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13991}{[S2]}

\subsection{Short English statement}
Apart from finitely many exceptions for each fixed positive epsilon, is c at most the radical of abc raised to the power one plus epsilon, when a and b are coprime positive integers with a+b=c?

\subsection{Sources}
\begin{description}
\item[S1] ULAM.AI and the UnsolvedMath Contributors, \emph{UnsolvedMath: A Curated Collection of Open Mathematics Problems}, record 1184 (NT-030). CC BY 4.0. \url{https://huggingface.co/datasets/ulamai/UnsolvedMath}.
\item[S2] Jared Duker Lichtman, \emph{The abc conjecture is true almost always}, arXiv:2505.13991 (2025), Section 1, the quantified conjecture preceding (1.1). \url{https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13991}.
\end{description}
